_note: The class of lines that change Explorer's Hidden or ShowSuperHidden setting, which the two write guards must catch, and the look-alikes they must leave: bounded by who writes such a line by accident (bounded_by) and not closed against every spelling, because a regex over C# and PowerShell cannot close an open spelling space; what the guards cannot see is pinned as 'miss' rows so that a change to it is seen. First enumerated by SL-091 review n2 (B01-B29, W01-W34) and widened by SL-103 (B30-B51, W35-W73: the RegistryRights overloads of OpenSubKey, PowerShell's string, cast and all-string opens, deletes, reg import, the registry-provider cmdlets). The class is bounded by who writes such a line by accident: in src, C# through Microsoft.Win32's registry API, the shell's own settings call with its set flag, or a Win32 or shlwapi registry write or delete declared and called; in tests/window, a window script's ItemProperty and Item cmdlets, reg.exe, the same .NET registry API from PowerShell (static and on a key, either quote, string or enum rights), and C# in an Add-Type block or the hook. ExplorerSettingsWriteRuleTests feeds every line, alone, to the guard of its scope: 'src' rows to ArchitectureRulesTests.TheAppNeverWritesExplorersSettings's patterns, read from that Fact (twinned in .taad/fitness.yaml), and 'window' rows to the settled entry 'no window case or hook changes Explorer's view settings', read from .taad/fitness.yaml. 'now' is what the guard does today: fire, quiet, or miss (a known limit of a tripwire on names, pinned so a change to it is seen: a key path, value name or rights held in a variable or constant, a call laid over two lines, a positional or abbreviated -Name, a write through a handle, command aliases, .reg content, regedit /s, WMI StdRegProv). 'before' is what the patterns the SL-091 design declared did with the same line, kept in the test as they were handed to build; it is not the code before SL-103. Every row whose 'before' is quiet and 'now' fire was closed after the design declared its patterns: by the SL-091 n2 fix for the rows up to B29 and W34, and by SL-103 for the ids in closed_by, which also names the commit and the command that fail them again. Fitness also blanks comments in .ps1 (#) and .cs (// and /* */) for the settled entry, and the twinned one matches comments too; no row here is a comment.

bounded_by.producers: Who writes a line that changes Explorer's Hidden or ShowSuperHidden by accident. In src: C# through Microsoft.Win32's registry API, the shell's settings call with its set flag, or a Win32 or shlwapi registry write or delete declared and called. In tests/window: a window script or the hook, using the registry-provider cmdlets, reg.exe, the same .NET registry API from PowerShell, or C# in an Add-Type block.
bounded_by.member: One line that opens Explorer\Advanced writable or with write-capable rights, sets, deletes, imports, copies, moves, renames or recreates its Hidden or ShowSuperHidden value or the key itself, in a spelling an ordinary producer reaches for.
bounded_by.write_capable_rights: RegistryRights.SetValue, WriteKey and FullControl, alone or combined. ReadKey and QueryValues cannot write, and CreateSubKey was measured unable to: RegSetValueExW on a handle opened with it returned 5 (SL-103, Sandbox), so B38 is quiet and the issue's marker, which included CreateSubKey, is deliberately not adopted for that word.
run_time_facts: A key opened with a write-capable RegistryRights value has a handle that changes Hidden through RegistryKey.FromHandle(handle).SetValue or RegSetValueExW (2 to 1 in the Sandbox), while a managed key.SetValue on it throws 'Cannot write to the registry key' (dotnet/runtime#113535, an open proposal).

PowerShell binds a non-empty quoted string second argument of OpenSubKey to the (string, bool) overload as $true, so 'ReadKey' and 'False' open the key fully writable (measured: state 4, managed SetValue ok).
Deleting Hidden changes the effective setting a fresh process reads through SHGetSetSettings (showAll 1 to 0).
New-Item -Force on an existing registry key recreates it empty (PowerShell/PowerShell#5444).
bounded_by.aliases_are_a_known_gap: Command aliases (rm, ri, del, sp, rp, clp, cli ...) are not matched, as in the RuleCases Remove-Item rule; the scripts under tests/window use none. W69 and W70 pin that.

outside_the_bound.why: A name, path or rights held in a variable or constant, a call over two lines, a write through a handle, command aliases and a positional -Name need a resolver, not a tripwire on names. A .reg file is inert until something imports it, and the import line fires; Fitness (taad_v3 backend/taad3/fitness.py content_hits) reads a UTF-16LE .reg, which is what reg export writes, as UTF-8, so no content pattern could see W53 or W54. regedit /s and WMI StdRegProv are deliberate routes, not spellings of the producer above.

bounded_by.not_pinned: Rights held in a variable (OpenSubKey(path, rights)), a using alias of RegistryRights, and a key path split over a parent open and a child call pass both guards and have no row yet; neither does a multi-line plant in the repo's real layout. Carried to the backlog as SC-308 (the census is not checked against the rows), SC-309 and SC-310.
bounded_by.next_step_if_this_reopens: Do not add a fourth batch of patterns (lesson #400). Use a spelling-independent check: a PowerShell AST check for tests/window, which P-004 already loads scripts through, and a symbol-level banned-API check for src. Filed, not built.
